title: The Twilight of Oil in an Age of Uncertainty: From a Vicious to a Virtuous Cycle
gist: A Carnegie commission paper argues that falling long-run hydrocarbon demand, accelerated by the 2026 Iran war and Hormuz risk, makes diversification urgent for MENA, yet GCC diversification remains shallow (Saudi private sector 43% of GDP vs 65% goal), middle-income exporters consume rents, and importers are in a debt-laden middle-income trap. It warns that power centralization, OPEC fragmentation after the UAE's exit, and crony state capitalism undermine reform, and calls for regional integration and re-homing of sovereign wealth.
